pr.title: Upgrade libpq to PostgreSQL 18.6 and MariaDB Connector/C to 3.4.11
pr.body:
## Summary

Brings the database client libraries up to their current supported releases and cleans up the stale vendored ones.

| Library | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| libpq | PostgreSQL 15.19 | **PostgreSQL 18.6** (supported until Nov 2030) |
| MariaDB Connector/C | 3.4.9 | **3.4.11** |
| libmysql | Vendored 5.7.38 (end of life, unused by the server build) | **Removed** |
| SQL Server Compact | Folder named `mssqlce3.5` | Renamed `mssqlce4.0`. The code was already 4.0 SP1, the final release |
| msado28 | Unchanged | Kept. It is the compile-time type library; ADO itself comes from Windows |

OpenSSL was checked as well: 3.5.9 is already the newest patch of the 3.5 LTS line (supported until Apr 2030), so it is unchanged.

## Changes

- **libpq build rewritten for Meson.** PostgreSQL 17 removed the `src\tools\msvc` build. `libraries/build-pgsql.ps1` now fetches pinned Meson 1.12.1, Ninja 1.13.2 and winflexbison 2.5.25 (checked against a recorded SHA-256), fails if libpq is configured without OpenSSL, and copies its output into the existing `Release\libpq` layout.
- **Windows 10 / Server 2016 minimum.** libpq from PostgreSQL 16 and later requires Windows 10, and `hMailServer.exe` imports libpq, so the installer's `MinVersion` is now `10.0`. Docs and the README were updated to match.
- **VM test runner.**
  - The upgrade environments now use the bundled `libmariadb.dll`.
  - The environment that existed only to test `libmysql.dll` is removed, and so are the Vista and 8.1 environments.
  - The server's runtime fallback to an administrator-supplied `libmysql.dll` is unchanged.
- The upgrade-pgsql, upgrade-mariadb and upgrade-openssl skills were updated for the new versions and recipe.

## Testing

- ✅ CI [Build run](https://github.com/jassifx/arzoiemail/actions/runs/39996210648):
  - libpq 18.6 and MariaDB 3.4.11 built from source.
  - hMailServer and the installer built.
  - The regression suite passed (it runs against SQL CE).
- ⚠️ The CI tests do not connect to PostgreSQL or MySQL. Before release, run the VMTestRunner PostgreSQL and MySQL environments, especially the 4.1.1 and 4.4.4 MySQL upgrade VMs, which now use the MariaDB client.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Inno Setup can move past 6.2.2 now that Vista is not supported.
- The bundled UCRT (10.0.14393) and `build/Test-DownlevelForwarders.ps1` exist only for pre-Windows 10 support and can be removed.

commit.message:
Upgrade libpq to PostgreSQL 18.6 and MariaDB Connector/C to 3.4.11

libpq
- Rewrite libraries\build-pgsql.ps1 for Meson, the only MSVC build system
  PostgreSQL ships since 17 removed src\tools\msvc. The script fetches pinned
  Meson 1.12.1, Ninja 1.13.2 and winflexbison 2.5.25 (SHA-256 checked) into
  %hMailServerLibs%\tools, fails unless libpq is configured with OpenSSL, and
  copies the output into the Release\libpq layout the project already uses.
- Pin PostgreSQL 18.6 (supported until November 2030) instead of 15.19.

Windows 10 minimum
- libpq from PostgreSQL 16 and later requires Windows 10, and hMailServer.exe
  imports it, so the installer's MinVersion is raised to 10.0. The system
  requirements page, README and VM test environments follow; the Vista and 8.1
  VM environments are removed.

MariaDB / libmysql
- Pin MariaDB Connector/C 3.4.11 instead of 3.4.9.
- Remove the vendored libmysql 5.7.38 (MySQL 5.7 is end of life). The server
  never compiled against it; only the VM test runner copied it in. The upgrade
  VM environments now run on the bundled libmariadb.dll, and the environment
  that existed only to exercise libmysql.dll is removed. The server's runtime
  fallback to an administrator-supplied libmysql.dll is unchanged.

SQL Server Compact
- Rename libraries\mssqlce3.5 to mssqlce4.0. The headers, the OLE DB provider
  and the bundled runtime (4.0.8876.1) are already SQL CE 4.0 SP1, its final
  release; the folder name was stale.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

issue.body:
## Summary

CI now also runs the full regression suite on MySQL, alongside the internal database and PostgreSQL. The MySQL and PostgreSQL connections write command parameters into the SQL themselves rather than binding them, so each needs its own run.

## Changes

- **`tests.yml`:** the `database` input also accepts `mysql`. The new step "Move the server to MySQL" uses the runner image's MySQL 8.0:
  - creates a data directory with `--initialize-insecure`, using an options file of its own (`--defaults-file`) so none of the image's option files apply;
  - installs and starts mysqld as a Windows service on port 3307;
  - runs `CreateExternalDatabase`, `SetDefaultDatabase` and `Reinitialize`, as DBSetup does.
- **`build.yml`:** new `test-mysql` job, "Tests (MySQL)".
- **`TestFixtureBase.TearDown`:** a failed test now prints its failure message and the errors the server logged, as it happens. The console runner only prints failures at the end of a run, and a run that hits the job timeout never gets there.

## What the first runs found

1. **MySQL stopped after the setup step.** The runner ends every process a step started when the step ends, so a mysqld started with `Start-Process` was gone before the tests began. Every test then failed in setup, after about 76 seconds of `Can't connect to server on '127.0.0.1' (10061)`, and the job hit its 120-minute timeout. mysqld now runs as a service, as PostgreSQL does. The cause only became visible through the TearDown output above.
2. **Writes were slow.** By default MySQL 8 waits for two disk flushes on every autocommit write. The options file therefore turns the binary log off and sets `innodb_flush_log_at_trx_commit=2`. On the Hyper-V test VM, a setting write went from 200 ms to 4.5 ms, and `API.UtilitiesTests` from 267 s to 26 s (17 s on the internal database). The database is thrown away with the runner, so durability doesn't matter.

## Verification

All three test jobs give the same result as the baseline:

| Run | Total | Passed | Failed | Inconclusive | Skipped |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tests (MySQL) | 1,294 | 1,185 | 0 | 34 | 75 |
| Tests (PostgreSQL) | 1,294 | 1,185 | 0 | 34 | 75 |
| Tests (internal) | 1,294 | 1,185 | 0 | 34 | 75 |

This gives a MySQL baseline for 1.1c (MySQL prepared statements). The publish job still depends only on the build and the internal-database tests.
